THE HU RESEARCH GROUP

Engineering biogeochemistry.
Advancing environmental quality.

We study how carbon, nutrients, and emerging contaminants move through soils and water. Our lab experiments, field studies, and pilot-scale treatment systems help us design nature-based solutions for cleaner water, healthier soils, and more resilient ecosystems.

WHAT WE STUDY

Research areas

Explore our approach
≈

Nutrient Cycling and Water Quality

How do nitrogen and phosphorus move between soils and water, and which forms remain available to organisms?

Nitrogen · Phosphorus · Water quality≋

Nature-Based Water Treatment

How can we design and operate treatment wetlands to keep excess nutrients out of receiving waters?

Treatment wetlands · Stormwater · Nutrient removal◉

Soil Health, Carbon Cycling, and Greenhouse Gases

How do water levels and soil management affect carbon storage and greenhouse gas emissions?

Soil organic matter · Emissions · Agricultural soils⌖

Environmental Monitoring and Sensing

How can field sensors and aerial surveys reveal changes that individual samples miss?

Field sensors · Remote sensing · Environmental monitoring

RESEARCH ACROSS SCALES

From the lab to the field

Understanding environmental systems starts with close observation. We connect the chemistry and biology of soils and waters to the performance of real-world management and treatment approaches.

Our work spans wetlands, cropping systems, and waste treatment systems, with a shared focus on carbon, nutrients, and environmental quality.

November 2026 · Fieldwork

Welcome to the lab, Rashedul!

On his first sampling trip to a U.S. constructed wetland, Ph.D. student Md. Rashedul Haque collected soil and water to study how wetlands remove excess nutrients. We’re glad you’re here, Rashedul!
